_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false = must not load; null = output-quality only.

evals.prompt: The phpunit job on my merge request is red: CurrencyConversionTest fails with 'Failed asserting that 2287 matches expected 1143.' My MR only changes a Blade view and a translation file. Can I just hit retry until it goes green and merge?
assertions: Checks whether the change touches the failing code and whether trunk's latest pipeline is green before deciding

Counts how often the same assertion failed on other pipelines or merge requests through the GitLab API (for example ci_recurrence.py or glab api over failed jobs and their traces) instead of calling it a one-off
Distinguishes retrying the job from starting a new pipeline on the same commit, and compares the image digest of a failing and a passing run
Recommends at most one rerun to unblock plus a flake ticket carrying the count, not retry-until-green
Names the likely mechanism class: values landing on the wrong row points at an unordered query or a positional fake

evals.prompt: I fixed our flaky upload test. It used to fail sometimes, so I bumped the wait before stopping the fake worker from 300 ms to 2 seconds. It passed three times locally. Good to merge?
assertions: Rejects the longer timer as a fix and has the test wait for a signal from the fake (a line it prints once its output is written) under an overall deadline
Proves the fix with many repeated runs (tens or hundreds), each with a per-run timeout, ideally under parallel load
Requires a break-check: reverting the fix or mutating the guarded behaviour must turn the test red
Does not accept three local passes as evidence

evals.prompt: Two builds of our CI testing image from commits that differ only in one test fixture are about 500 KB apart, and the last layer (COPY . .) is bigger in the second one. Could something have sneaked into the image, and could that explain our flaky test?
assertions: Checks whether the failing and passing pipelines ran the same image digest before suspecting the image
Compares layer digests from the manifests and the differing layers' file contents rather than image sizes

Explains that BuildKit re-adds files with unchanged content when their mtime changed (COPY cache keys ignore mtime while the layer differ compares it), so builds are not byte-reproducible across checkouts
Runs or recommends layer_diff.py or an equivalent content comparison that ignores mtime

evals.prompt: I set up GitLab CI for our PHP library using the same CI components our apps use. Every merge request pipeline now shows 'failed' with 0 jobs and no log. What is going on?
assertions: Reads the pipeline's yaml_errors (REST) or errorMessages (GraphQL) instead of looking for a job log
Explains that jobs without rules default to except merge_requests, so a job another job needs is missing from merge request pipelines
Proposes matching rules or workflow rules in the project's own .gitlab-ci.yml, noting that rules arriving through include do not count
Notes that app components which run inside the application's testing image do not fit a library

evals.prompt: Two commits that were on main yesterday are gone and a release was cut without them. Nobody admits to force-pushing. How do we find out what happened?
assertions: Builds one UTC timeline from the forge activity feed, the SHAs CI runs fetched, mirror activity, every clone's remote-tracking reflog and agent session push commands
Uses reflog entries such as 'update by push' and 'forced-update' to place local pushes and rewrites
States that a ref change with no feed entry, no CI run and no client push points inside the forge, such as a mirror sync
Pins the lost commit on a rescue branch before any repair and avoids an unagreed force-push

evals.prompt: Our pre-commit hook (php-cs-fixer, phpstan, prettier --check, eslint) takes about 45 seconds. Static analysis is surely the slow part. Make it faster.
assertions: Times each step separately and records the machine load before choosing what to optimise or claiming a speed-up
Uses Prettier and ESLint caches with a cache location keyed on the lockfile hash, because neither cache key tracks plugin versions
Keeps the CI check uncached as the gate

evals.prompt: Is PR #212 ready to merge? Check the approvals, whether the branch is up to date with main, and that the description links the ticket.
assertions: Does not load the flaky-ci-forensics skill
